title: consolidate-gpu-lease-policy-and-vpc-peering-tf-migrations
author: Evan Chen
release_notes: Consolidates GPU lease/reservation TF module, introduces idempotent VPC peering module and state migrator v2. Updates IAM scoping for tenant-bound GPU roles. Migration tool included for safe in-place tfstate transformation; no runtime API changes expected.
description:
Context: Private installer deployments have multiple ad-hoc TF modules for GPU nodepool leases, IAM roles and VPC peering created during early iterations. This fragmented layout makes cross-account peering and tfstate operations brittle during upgrades.

Motivation: Consolidate the GPU-lease semantics into a single, tenant-scoped module, centralize IAM scoping rules, and introduce an idempotent VPC peering module plus a tfstate migrator to safely move existing state to the new layout without downtime.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces modules/gpu-reservation (replaces legacy gpu-lease and gpu-subnet-claim modules). The new module exposes an immutable reservation object and a lightweight lease-to-reservation shim for backward compatibility. 2) Adds modules/vpc-peering-idempotent which performs peer creation with edge-case retry handling for cloud API eventual consistency and exposes explicit peering IDs for rollback. 3) Adds tooling/migrator/tfstate-migrator-v2 which: - Performs a dry-run mapping of old resources to new module addresses - Creates a deterministic state rewrite plan (no resource re-creates) - Applies state move operations against a locked remote backend with verification checksums and post-migration validation hooks 4) Tightens IAM role scoping: new roles use tenant-scoped path prefixes and least-privilege polices for nodepool role and peering management. 5) Adds migration docs and a staged rollout checklist.

Rollout plan (short): - Stage 0: Run migrator dry-run in staging and validate resource counts and checksums - Stage 1: Run migrator against staging state, apply new TF, smoke test nodepool creation and GC - Stage 2: Coordinate a rolling migration window for production with customer ops, snapshot state, run migrator, apply TF, monitor.

Backout plan: - If post-migration checks fail, use the migrator snapshot to revert state, or restore backend snapshot and re-apply old TF.

Checklist: - [x] Module refactor and new module tests - [x] Migrator implementation with dry-run - [x] Integration smoke tests (local k8s + mocked cloud) - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] IAM least-privilege validation - [x] Reviewer approvals

Testing notes: ran migrator dry-run on an internal staging tenant (tenant-e2e-03) and validated mapping (10 nodepools -> reservations) and cross-account peering reconciliation.

Observability: added telemetry counters for migrator: dry_run_map_count, moved_resources_count, validation_fail_count.

Risks and mitigation: - Risk: state move mistakes — mitigated by deterministic mapping and checksum/verifier hooks - Risk: peer acceptance race — mitigated by idempotent peering retries and explicit peering-id outputs - Risk: IAM scope regression — mitigated by separate IAM role testing in staging
